summary: Analysis of the 14-day telemetry and active AAPS profile demonstrates exceptionally stable glycemic control with a Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL) of 99.7%, average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, coefficient of variation of 12.9%, and 0.0% time below range. Basal rates, insulin-to-carb ratios, and insulin sensitivity factors are well-tuned. Current AAPS SMB and UAM settings operate smoothly with no unsafe insulin stacking.

analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry quality is complete with 1,345 CGM entries over 14 days, 100% data coverage, and zero gaps greater than 15 minutes.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 valid CGM entries across 14 days; coverage_percent = 100.0; largest_gap_minutes = 15.0.

analysis_steps.findings: Outstanding safety profile with zero recorded hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) and minimal time above range (0.3%).
analysis_steps.evidence: Time in Range = 99.7%, Time Below Range = 0.0%, Time Above Range = 0.3%, Mean = 117.0 mg/dL, CV = 12.9%.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight and fasting basal segments maintain flat glucose trajectories around 100-106 mg/dL without loop over-correction.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly glucose averages overnight (00:00-06:00) range between 102.3 mg/dL and 107.5 mg/dL with 100% TIR.

analysis_steps.findings: CR and ISF settings are appropriate. Postprandial returns to target occur reliably within 3 to 5 hours across all meal types.
analysis_steps.evidence: Meal bolus windows show 240-minute glucose changes between -11 mg/dL and +8 mg/dL relative to pre-meal start.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM algorithms function efficiently to trim postprandial peaks without inducing late-phase hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_interval_minutes=3, max_smb_basal_minutes=45, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 with 0% hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits (max basal 2.4 U/h, max IOB 8.0 U) provide safe guardrails relative to profile basal rates (0.85-1.05 U/h).
analysis_steps.evidence: Max basal is 2.3x highest basal segment (1.05 U/h); max IOB (8.0 U) safely accommodates largest meal boluses (5.8 U).

analysis_steps.findings: Prebolus timing (10-20 minutes) and immediate bolus splits (60-70%) align well with meal absorption profiles.
analysis_steps.evidence: 28 meal treatments analyzed; average 120m rise is +35 to +57 mg/dL for fast carbs and +62 to +70 mg/dL for high-fat brunch, fully recovering by 240m.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared e-carbs for high-fat weekend brunches accurately model extended carbohydrate absorption, preventing secondary spikes.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekend brunch (68g carbs, 20g e-carbs over 120m) achieves 111-113 mg/dL glucose by 360 minutes post-meal.

analysis_steps.findings: All parameters are appropriately configured. No profile parameter changes are required; recommendation focus is to maintain current settings and verify unpopulated client UI toggles.
analysis_steps.evidence: 14-day TIR of 99.7%, zero hypoglycemia, excellent postprandial recovery, and well-balanced safety parameters.

strengths: Exceptional 99.7% Time in Range with zero recorded hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL).
Highly stable overnight basal control maintaining glucose within target (100-110 mg/dL).
Effective meal management strategies for both fast-acting breakfast and mixed-composition brunch meals.
Well-proportioned AAPS safety limits preventing insulin stacking or over-delivery.

recommendations.title: Maintain Current Profile & Settings
recommendations.description: Current basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA, and target segments produce optimal glycemic control (99.7% TIR, 0% TBR). Maintain all existing profile parameters.

recommendations.title: Verify App Settings for Unpopulated Toggles
recommendations.description: Confirm in the AAPS user interface that SMB activation conditions and Autosens toggles match your intended configuration.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current basal, CR, ISF, target, and DIA settings unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Glycemic outcomes are exemplary with 99.7% Time in Range, 0.0% Time Below Range, average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, and CV of 12.9%. Basal rates accurately reflect fasting requirements.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Re-evaluate CGM metrics after 14 days or if daily routines/meal compositions change significantly.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Administer a 15-20 minute prebolus with a ~70% immediate split for standard fast-carb meals, relying on profile CR and active SMB/UAM automation. Use e-carbs (20g, 120m duration, +15m offset) for higher-fat mixed meals to manage delayed absorption without early insulin stacking.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Telemetry shows consistent recovery to target range (100-115 mg/dL) by 240-360 minutes post-meal across all meal types with zero recorded hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Monitor 2-hour postprandial glucose during high-fat weekend brunches to confirm whether small variations in prebolus timing affect the peak height.

exceptions.suggestion: 10-minute prebolus, 60% immediate bolus, 20g e-carbs with 120-minute duration and 15-minute start offset.
exceptions.rationale: Prevents early over-bolusing and allows UAM/SMB to manage delayed fat/protein rise safely without late hypoglycemia.
Aligns with morning insulin sensitivity to blunt early glucose rise while bringing glucose smoothly to target by 240 minutes.

implementation_steps: Review current setup and confirm all active profile parameters match the existing configuration.
Verify in the AAPS app interface that SMB activation conditions and sensitivity toggles match intended settings.
Continue following established prebolus and e-carb timing for weekday breakfast and weekend brunch meals.
Re-evaluate data after 14 to 30 days or following any significant change in routine or diet.
education: A 99.7% Time in Range with 0.0% Time Below Range indicates an exceptionally well-tuned profile and automation setup.
